decision: Preserve live durable claim leases across qrexec process-per-call service invocations and enforce lease expiry on worker mutations.
context: The qrexec service starts a fresh coordinator process for each request. The default MissionQueue restore behavior treats every process start as crash recovery and clears running ownership, which makes a valid claim token unusable on the following complete/heartbeat call.

approaches.name: Treat every qrexec invocation as crash recovery
approaches.correctness: Poor for distributed workers because claim ownership is cleared before the next worker mutation.
approaches.robustness: Strong crash reset semantics but incompatible with process-per-call transport lifecycle.
approaches.regressionRisk: High for real worker claim-to-complete flows.

approaches.name: Persist and restore live leases until leaseUntil
approaches.correctness: Strong: workerId + per-claim leaseToken remain valid only for the persisted lease window; expired mutations are rejected.
approaches.robustness: Strong for stateless qrexec calls and preserves existing crash-recovery behavior elsewhere by making the behavior opt-in.
approaches.latency: No additional network round trip and negligible local checks.
approaches.resourceUse: No daemon or external database required.
approaches.regressionRisk: Low because the default restore mode is unchanged and qrexec opts in explicitly.

approaches.name: Long-lived coordinator daemon behind qrexec
approaches.robustness: Introduces daemon lifecycle, restart, supervision and additional attack-surface concerns.
approaches.latency: Potentially lower per operation after startup.

qa: MissionQueue regression: live lease and fencing token survive restore when preserveRunningLeasesOnRestore=true.
MissionQueue regression: complete/heartbeat reject an expired lease even before another worker claims.

qrexec service regression: a deliberately complex build/code fixture routes orchestrator -> planner -> coder, and each agent claims in one process then completes in a fresh process using the returned fencing token.
failuresAndLessons: Process-boundary durability is not sufficient if process lifecycle semantics are conflated with crash semantics.
A stateless transport service must persist lease ownership across clean invocations; crash recovery and clean service termination are different events.
Lease expiry must be checked on mutation, not only when another claim happens, or a late worker can mutate after leaseUntil.

QA #159 initially failed at the planner claim because the test text selected coder but did not satisfy the planner routing rule. The strongest fix was to make the fixture explicitly complex (build + code) so it exercises the intended orchestrator/planner/coder chain; changing production routing or deleting the planner assertion would have weakened correctness coverage.
safety: Synthetic defensive orchestration only. No real financial transactions or external side effects are enabled by this change.
